claims.text: GF is by advance request only — 「グルテンフリー対応できます。事前にご連絡ください」 — so the default meal is not prepared in a gluten-free workflow. Wheat items (chapati/roti/naan on North Indian thali, papad, barley non-alcoholic beer) and possibly wheat-containing asafoetida (hing) are used in the same small kitchen, so cross-contact is a real risk unless the reserved GF plate is made.
South Indian cooking here uses no soy sauce; seasoning is via sambar/rasam spice bases, so wheat-in-soy-sauce is not a typical exposure. Not explicitly documented — confirm on reservation.
Kitchen is 100% vegan (all-vegan, no meat/fish/dairy/egg and no garlic or onion), so there is no animal-product cross-contact risk.
Reservation-only with English-speaking staff and an English menu; the venue explicitly offers gluten-free accommodation when notified in advance, indicating willingness to handle dietary requests.

Fully vegan, no garlic/onion, largely rice- and lentil-based South Indian cuisine that is naturally low in wheat, plus a stated willingness to do gluten-free on advance notice — a good starting point for a celiac if arranged carefully.

name: TADACHIYA cafe THE GATE (タダチヤ カフェ ザ ゲート)

claims.text: The full menu (rice-flour churros, soft-serve, coffee) contains no wheat item, so there is nothing wheat-based to contaminate the fryer — but the venue makes no dedicated-fryer or dedicated-utensil statement.
Wheat-allergy blogger lists it only as a researched GF rice-flour churro spot and did not visit or verify cross-contact herself.
No soy sauce used — this is a sweets/coffee café with no savory soy-seasoned dishes.
Churro dough and sundaes contain egg and dairy; only black coffee is plant-based, so vegan cross-contact is a broad concern.
Venue posts a plain allergen list (egg, rice flour, milk) but publishes no allergy-handling or cross-contact protocol; ask staff directly.
«長野県産の米粉を使った自家製のオリジナル生地» — dough is made from Nagano-grown rice flour, and the posted allergens are only egg, rice flour and milk, with no wheat listed.
Churros are made to order one at a time, so a fresh batch can be requested.

name: Temariya Shinshu-Matsumoto Baumkuchen Kobo (信州松本バウムクーヘン工房 てまりや)

claims.text: Marketed as 100% rice-flour baumkuchen but no explicit wheat-free/dedicated-equipment statement found; confirm the specific product and shared-roller risk before buying.
Sweets retailer — no soy-sauce dishes.
Products contain egg and butter; not vegan.
Featured on a wheat-allergy blogger's Matsumoto GF tour as a rice-flour baumkuchen option.
Signature line uses 100% Shinshu rice flour / brown-rice flour instead of wheat and is branded gluten-free.

name: A double prime (a″／エーダブルプライム)

claims.text: All products are rice-flour based and 『こちらで売られている商品すべてがグルテンフリー』; no wheat flour is used on the premises, so there is no in-house wheat cross-contact source.
Not applicable — this is a sweets/baked-goods shop; no soy-sauce-based savory dishes.
Dairy and egg are used in many items (custard, cheese terrine, butter cookies); not a vegan kitchen.
The baker is a registered dietitian (管理栄養士), and the shop is built entirely around gluten-free rice-flour baking.
100% rice-flour, fully gluten-free product line — one of the safest celiac sweet stops in Nagoya.
Also sold at Social Tower Market pop-ups as 『米粉のスコーン・焼き菓子』.

name: Gluten Free BITTE (グルテンフリーBITTE)

claims.text: Shop states it is 「小麦不使用・完全グルテンフリーのお店」 with 「コンタミネーションを徹底管理した」 — wheat-free with contamination strictly managed; no wheat baked on site.
Bakery (breads and chiffon cakes) — soy sauce not a factor in the product line.
Eggs and dairy are used in some items (e.g. chiffon cakes); each product is labelled for 小麦・卵・乳製品 so vegans can screen.
Owner-run by a person with gluten intolerance; reservation-only so needs can be discussed when ordering via LINE/Instagram.
Entire facility is wheat-free/GF (no wheat baked on premises), founded and run by a celiac-adjacent (gluten-intolerant) owner.
Per-item allergen labelling for wheat, egg and dairy.

GF (rice) pasta is boiled in the same pot as wheat noodles; the shop states it cannot guarantee for allergies. GF sweets use both 米粉 and そば粉 (buckwheat), so shared confection equipment plus a separate buckwheat allergen apply.
Dairy, meat and seafood are pervasive on the menu; vegan handling not addressed.
The shop is upfront about the shared-pot limitation, which suggests some allergy awareness — ask staff to steer you to the dedicated gluten-free baked goods rather than the pasta swap.
Maintains a dedicated gluten-free cake and baked-goods line (米粉/そば粉), also sold nationwide via BASE.
「グルテンフリー（小麦の取り扱いなし）」 — the shop handles no wheat on the premises, so there is no in-house wheat cross-contact source.
「当店の商品はすべて小麦・乳製品・卵不使用です」 — every product is made without wheat, dairy or egg.
Not applicable — bakery; no soy-sauce-based dishes served.
No dairy or egg is used anywhere in the facility, so vegan cross-contact from within the kitchen is effectively nil; sweeteners are plant-based (kibi/beet sugar, maple syrup).
The entire shop is purpose-built as an allergen-free (wheat/dairy/egg) bakery, so allergen avoidance is the default operating model rather than a special request.
Rated ★★★★★ on the JP gluten-free guide with the note 「小麦の取り扱いなし」 (no wheat handled).
All products are simultaneously gluten-free, dairy-free and egg-free — fully suitable for celiac and vegan diners.
Wheat-containing 80%-rice-flour breads and the 100% rice-flour GF line are baked in the same kitchen; the komeko-palette guide notes no published contamination-prevention protocol.
The 100% rice-flour line is made without egg or dairy, but shares equipment with standard breads.
Pre-order system by phone/email the day before allows requesting the 100% gluten-free items; confirm separation directly.
Maintains an explicit 米粉100% gluten-free line free of wheat, egg and dairy, additive-free.
